title: My prayer, my life, my death
hookLine: say, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death are for Allah (6:162)

lines: SAID AT THE START OF THE PRAYER.
cards: People write mission statements for companies, for nonprofits, for their own lives, and plenty end up in a drawer. Surah six closes with one that fits in a single breath, and it isn't in a drawer.
Sahih Muslim reports the Prophet ﷺ saying it at the very start of the prayer, right after Allahu akbar and before al-Fatiha, and some Muslims open their prayer with it today.
For them, it's the first thing said once the prayer begins.

teach.b: Verse one-sixty-two, in Pickthall's words: “Say: Lo! my worship and my sacrifice and my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the Worlds.” In Arabic, four short words with the same ending, the i that means my.
Salati: my prayer. Nusuki: my sacrifice, my acts of devotion; the word covers the offering at Eid and, for some commentators, every rite of worship.
Mahyaya: my living. Mamati: my dying. Notice how the list grows.
It starts with prayer, a few minutes a day. Then devotion, a bit wider. Then my whole life: the commute, the dishes, the job, the friendships.
Then even the moment of death.
Nothing is left over as mine alone. The next verse adds: He has no partner. This I am commanded, and I am the first of those who submit.
Ali is the one who reports it, in Muslim's collection: the Prophet's opening joined these verses with the line from five days ago, I have turned my face toward Him.
Three verses later, surah six closes, saying Allah made people successors on the earth, raising some above others in rank to test them in what He has given.

teach.h: FOR ALLAH, LORD OF THE WORLDS.
teach.b: So al-An'am began with darkness and light, walked through a leaf, the stars, a seed, an eye that can't see Him, a list of duties, and ends here: the whole of a life, handed over in a sentence.

how: Some Muslims recite 6:162–163, often together with 6:79, as part of the opening supplication of the prayer after the first takbir; practice varies by school, and some use a shorter opening instead.

o: a private request for something you really need
the call to prayer that opens each new day
salati: prayer, first of four things given to Allah

games.q: inside the verse — tap the pairs.

Ali reports it in Muslim's collection, joined with 6:79.
the verse dedicates only acts of worship to Allah

games.q: you've just said Allahu akbar to begin the prayer. in the opening supplication Ali reported, what comes soon after?
o: I have turned my face… my prayer, my sacrifice, my living, my dying are for Allah.
games.why: the supplication in Muslim's collection joins 6:79 and 6:162–163, said before al-Fatiha.

practice: Walk through your day in four steps, as the verse does: any moment of prayer or stillness, any act of giving, the ordinary hours of work, errands, meals and people, and then, gently, the fact that this day is one of a number.
If you pray, you can say the verse itself, in Arabic or in English; if not, sum up who the day is for in one plain sentence of your own.

wordCard.voice: My prayer. Salati, in surah six, verse one-sixty-two: my prayer, my devotion, my living and my dying, all for Allah. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: my prayer. salah (prayer) + i (my), from 6:162.

carryVoice: Your line: all of it for him. The dishes and the drive belong in the sentence too. Day four hundred five.
